info.name: Synap Mentor - Mobile Push & Phone Verification
info.description:
Mobile app (iOS/Android) endpoints for FCM push notifications, plus every solver phone-verification endpoint, including the ones changed on 2026-10-24.

**How to use**
1. Set `baseUrl`, `appPlatform` (android | ios) and `appVersion`.
2. Log in natively (POST /auth/login with X-App-Platform android/ios — tokens come back in the body; see the main collection) and paste the access token into `accessToken`.
3. Push: set `fcmToken` to the device's Firebase token, then call register. Call remove before logout.
4. Phone (solver): phone-policy → phone-start (send Firebase the returned `data.phone`) → Firebase SMS on the device → verify-phone-firebase with the Firebase ID token in `firebaseIdToken`. Report a wrong code with phone-failure; call phone-start again before every resend.

Requests marked **[CHANGED 2026-10-24]** have a "Changed" section at the top of their description; **[unchanged]** ones are copied from `docs/Synap-Mentor-API.postman_collection.json`. Native clients send no CSRF header. Error bodies differ per handler: KYC endpoints use `message`, push and profile endpoints use `error`.

Full push behaviour: `docs/mobile/push_notification_apis.json`.

**Added 2026-10-24 (app integration)**: solver content edit, solver price tiers, session extension, anonymous session price (2×), seeker review shown to solver, podcasts, solver events edit. Traced from code, then live-tested on 2026-10-25 (see each request's "Live test" table). `/seeker/*` requests use `seekerAccessToken`; solver requests use `accessToken`; `/public/*` need no token. Fill `sessionId`, `bookingId`, `contentId`, `eventId`, `solverId` as you go. Every request lists its errors as saved example responses.

request.description:
Register or refresh this device's FCM token against the current login session.

**When to call:** after login, on every app start, and whenever Firebase issues a new token (onTokenRefresh).
**Auth:** Bearer access token + live session. Seeker or solver. No KYC level required. No CSRF header (native client).
**Only from the app:** `X-App-Platform` must be `ios`/`android` and must equal `platform` in the body. Browsers are refused (CSRF 403 before the handler, or 400 below).
**Rate limit:** RATE_LIMIT_PUSH_TOKEN_PER_HOUR (default 30) per user per hour, counted separately from /remove.
**Maintenance:** not exempt — 503 MAINTENANCE_MODE while mobile maintenance is on.

**Request body**
```json
{
  "token": "string, required, 20-4096 chars, FCM alphabet only: letters, digits, _ - :",
  "platform": "string, required: android | ios (must equal X-App-Platform)"
}
```

**Server behaviour**
- The token is bound to this login session. It only receives pushes while that session is live (not revoked, not expired, account active), so logout, logout-all, password change, role switch, deactivate, delete and bans stop pushes automatically.
- Same token registered by another account (phone changed hands) → it moves to the new account.
- At most PUSH_MAX_DEVICES_PER_USER (default 10) tokens per user; the least recently seen is dropped.
- Dead tokens (session ended, or unseen for PUSH_STALE_TOKEN_DAYS, default 60) are deleted the next time this user's tokens are registered or used.

**Push the app receives**
- `notification.title` / `notification.body` (title ≤ 100 chars, body ≤ 200; chat has no body).
- `data.type`: the notification type, e.g. `community.new_message`, `task_due_reminder`, `notification.in_app`, `chat.message`.
- `data.id`: `chat.message` → session id (open that chat); `notification.in_app` → Notifications-page item id (open the Notifications page); anything else → bell notification id (as in GET /users/notifications).
- Android: channel id `updates`, priority high — create the `updates` channel at app start. iOS: sound `default`.
- Money/OTP text never appears: such notifications arrive as "You have an account update" / "Open the app to see the details."

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/mobile_app_handler.go MobileAppHandler.RegisterPushToken`
**Live check 2026-10-24:** 200, 400 (both), 401 and 429 verified with a throwaway native login.

Returns the dial code and digit bounds the KYC phone step must enforce, derived from the solver's profile country.

**Auth:** True | **Roles:** solver | **CSRF header:** no
**Middleware that runs:** AuthMiddleware; RequireRole(solver); TimezoneMiddleware; RequireFeatureAccess(kyc)
**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/kyc_handler.go:2183 KYCHandler.GetSolverPhonePolicy`

**Response 200** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "success": "boolean",
  "country_configured": "boolean",
  "country": "string (omitempty)",
  "country_iso": "string (omitempty)",
  "dial_code": "string (omitempty)",
  "min_digits": "integer (omitempty)",
  "max_digits": "integer (omitempty)",
  "national_number": "string (omitempty)",
  "phone_verified": "boolean",
  "message": "string (omitempty)"
}
```
_No data wrapper. If profile country missing/unmapped/no phone rule: country_configured=false, message='Set your country in Profile before verifying your mobile number.'. national_number = profile phone digits with dial code stripped, only when within min..max digits. Every non-200 body written by this KYC handler is domain.KYCResponse {"success":false,"message":"..."} (key `message`, not `error`) unless stated otherwise._

- 403: `This feature is currently restricted for your account | This feature is temporarily unavailable platform-wide | This feature is temporarily unavailable for your role` - RequireFeatureAccess(kyc) finds feature 'kyc' blocked for the user/role. Body: {success:false, restricted:true, feature:'kyc', error, source, reason?, expires_at? | permanent:true}. Fails open on lookup error.

request.description:
### Changed 2026-10-24
- **409** when the number is already the verified phone of another solver account (checked before any SMS is sent). Body has `message` and `error` (same text) plus `data` = the OTP channel state.
- On success the server now **remembers this number** for the account. `verify-phone-firebase` only accepts a Firebase token for this exact number, so the app must send Firebase the `data.phone` returned here (canonical E.164) and must call phone-start again before every send/resend.
- **Live check 2026-10-24:** 200 and 409 below captured with a throwaway solver.

---
Pre-flight before the browser asks Firebase for an SMS: enforces phone-channel lockout and validates the number against the profile country, returning the canonical E.164 number.

**Auth:** True | **Roles:** solver | **CSRF header:** yes
**Middleware that runs:** AuthMiddleware; RequireRole(solver); TimezoneMiddleware; RequireFeatureAccess(kyc)
**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/kyc_handler.go:2208 KYCHandler.StartSolverPhoneVerification`

**Request body** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "phone": "string"
}
```
**Required:** phone
**Validation:**
- phone: required,min=4,max=20
- must normalise to the profile country's dial code and digit length (utils.ValidatePhoneForCountry + dial-code match)
- email must already be verified and phone not yet verified

**Response 200** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "success": "boolean",
  "data": {
    "phone": "string (E.164)",
    "otp_state": {
      "channel": "string enum: email|phone",
      "resends_used": "integer",
      "resends_max": "integer",
      "resends_remaining": "integer",
      "failed_attempts": "integer",
      "failed_max": "integer",
      "attempts_remaining": "integer",
      "locked": "boolean",
      "locked_until": "string<date-time> | null (omitempty)",
      "retry_after": "integer (omitempty)",
      "lock_reason": "string (omitempty) enum: failed_attempts|resend_limit",
      "used": "integer",
      "max": "integer",
      "remaining": "integer"
    }
  }
}
```
_Every non-200 body written by this KYC handler is domain.KYCResponse {"success":false,"message":"..."} (key `message`, not `error`) unless stated otherwise._

**Endpoint-specific errors**
- 403: `This feature is currently restricted for your account | This feature is temporarily unavailable platform-wide | This feature is temporarily unavailable for your role` - RequireFeatureAccess(kyc) finds feature 'kyc' blocked for the user/role. Body: {success:false, restricted:true, feature:'kyc', error, source, reason?, expires_at? | permanent:true}. Fails open on lookup error.
- 400: `Invalid input` - bind failure
- 400: `Enter your mobile number.` - validation failure
- 429: `Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.` - phone channel locked (3 resends or 3 failed verifies within 24h arms a 24h lockout), OR the 'phone_init' start counter exhausted (MaxPhoneVerificationStarts = 4 per 24h; checked after the number validates). Body {success:false,error,code:'OTP_LOCKED',retry_after:int seconds,locked_until:date-time|null,data:OTPChannelState (phone)}; Retry-After header set when >0
- 400: `set your country in Profile before verifying your mobile number | phone number does not match your profile country | Phone number ... (length/required messages) | email must be verified before phone verification | phone already verified, cannot re-verify` - country/length/state problems; body {success:false,message,error,data:OTPChannelState}
- 500: `Could not start phone verification. Please try again.` - solver not found, no kyc_light row (ErrKYCSessionNotFound 'verification session not found' matches none of the 400 substrings), lockout read failure, phone_init counter DB failure

**Side effects:** Consumes one 'phone_init' start in kyc_otp_resend_attempts (4 per 24h; the 4th succeeds and arms a 24h lock) once lockout, state and number checks pass. No SMS is sent server-side.

**Live check:** not_run - state-changing endpoint; live run was limited to read-only GETs

**Changed since 2026-10-02:**
- side effect changed: each successful pre-flight now consumes the 'phone_init' counter (MaxPhoneVerificationStarts = 4 per 24h); previously no counter was charged
- new 429 OTP_LOCKED cause: phone_init start cap exhausted

**Listed in:** solver: `POST /api/v1/solver/kyc/light/phone-start` (docs/audit/solver_endpoints.md:131)

### Changed 2026-10-24
- **400** `this number does not match the one you requested a code for — request a new code and try again` when the number Firebase verified differs from the last phone-start number for this account, or phone-start was never called. Fix: call phone-start, then send the SMS to the returned `data.phone`.

- **Live check 2026-10-24:** the 400 "Phone verification failed" path (junk token, reaches Firebase) was captured live. The two new errors need a real Firebase SMS token and are traced from code.

Completes solver light KYC by verifying a Firebase phone ID token, checking country/lockout, saving the verified number and setting level to light.

**Auth:** True | **Roles:** solver | **CSRF header:** yes
**Middleware that runs:** AuthMiddleware; RequireRole(solver); TimezoneMiddleware; RequireFeatureAccess(kyc)
**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/kyc_handler.go:1621 KYCHandler.VerifySolverPhoneFirebase`

**Request body** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "firebase_token": "string",
  "phone_country_code": "string (omitempty)"
}
```
**Required:** firebase_token
**Validation:**
- firebase_token: required
- phone_country_code: omitempty,max=5 (accepted but ignored; dial code derived from profile country)

**Response 200** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "success": "boolean",
  "message": "string"
}
```
_message = 'Phone verified via Firebase. Light KYC verification completed.' Every non-200 body written by this KYC handler is domain.KYCResponse {"success":false,"message":"..."} (key `message`, not `error`) unless stated otherwise._

**Endpoint-specific errors**
- 403: `This feature is currently restricted for your account | This feature is temporarily unavailable platform-wide | This feature is temporarily unavailable for your role` - RequireFeatureAccess(kyc) finds feature 'kyc' blocked for the user/role. Body: {success:false, restricted:true, feature:'kyc', error, source, reason?, expires_at? | permanent:true}. Fails open on lookup error.
- 400: `Invalid input` - bind failure
- 400: `Firebase token is required.` - validation failure
- 429: `Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.` - channel locked (3 resends or 3 failed verifies within 24h arms a 24h lockout; key = user+channel). Body {success:false,error,code:'OTP_LOCKED',retry_after:int seconds,locked_until:date-time|null,data:OTPChannelState}; Retry-After header set when >0
- 400: `set your country in Profile before verifying your mobile number | phone number does not match your profile country` - ErrProfileCountryMissing / ErrPhoneCountryMismatch
- 400: `No active verification session. Please start verification first.` - no kyc_light row
- 409: `phone already verified, cannot re-verify` - kyc_light.phone_verified already true
- 400: `email must be verified before phone verification` - email step not done
- 400: `Phone verification failed. Please try again.` - Firebase token rejected (counted as a failed attempt)
- 500: `<raw error string>` - Firebase not configured ('firebase phone verification is not configured'), solver not found, 'no phone number found in Firebase token', ValidatePhoneForCountry length errors ('Phone number for this country must be ...'), lockout read failure, DB errors

**Side effects:** Rejected token increments phone failure counter; on success records external OTP success atomically (re-checks lockout), updates solvers.phone (E.164) and phone_country_code (derived), marks kyc_light phone verified and sets KYC level to 'light'.

### Changed 2026-10-24
- `phone` can no longer be changed here. The verified number is set only by mobile verification and changed only by support (admin `POST /admin/users/:user_id/phone`).
- Sending the stored number again, or an empty string, is accepted and changes nothing (the number is never cleared from here). Any other number → **400** `Your mobile number can only be changed by support. Contact support if it needs to change`.
- **Live check 2026-10-24:** both captured with a throwaway solver.

---
Partially updates the solver's profile fields (country once only, timezone validated against country, bio policy, DOB policy).

**Auth:** True | **Roles:** solver | **CSRF header:** yes
**Middleware that runs:** AuthMiddleware; RequireRole(solver); TimezoneMiddleware
**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/solver_profile_handler.go:107 SolverProfileHandler.UpdateProfile`

**Request body** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "first_name": "string (omitempty)",
  "last_name": "string (omitempty)",
  "bio": "string (omitempty)",
  "phone": "string (omitempty, E.164)",
  "phone_country_code": "string (omitempty)",
  "date_of_birth": "string<date> (omitempty)",
  "country": "string (omitempty)",
  "city": "string (omitempty)",
  "gender": "string (omitempty) enum: male|female|other|prefer_not_to_say",
  "spoken_languages": [
    "string"
  ],
  "timezone": "string (omitempty, IANA)"
}
```
**Validation:**
- empty strings for every *string field are treated as absent; gender lower-cased
- tags: first_name/last_name min=1,max=100; bio max=1000; phone e164; phone_country_code max=5; date_of_birth datetime=2006-01-02; country min=2,max=100; city min=2,max=100; gender oneof; spoken_languages max=25 items; timezone max=50 -> 400 with utils.FormatValidationError text, e.g. 'bio must be at most 1000 characters' (multiple joined with '; ')
- bio (when changed): trimmed, utils.ValidateBio (30-1000 chars, prose) -> 400 with rule text
- country can only be set when none stored; must be a known country with currency ('Please select your country from the list'); currency derived
- timezone canonicalised; must load and contain '/' ('Please select a valid timezone') and be in the country ('The selected timezone is not in your country. ...'); with no timezone sent and stored tz outside the country, the country's primary zone is written
- date_of_birth: utils.ValidateDateOfBirth (age 13..100, not future) - its error is NOT wrapped as a validation error, so a bad DOB returns 500
- first_name/last_name/phone/city/gender/spoken_languages are written as sent without further checks; no change -> no write, still 200

**Response 200** (application/json) - field types from code:
```json
{
  "success": "boolean",
  "message": "string (\"Profile updated successfully\")"
}
```
_data is nil and omitted (omitempty). solverProfileRestrict (RequireFeatureAccess(profile_edit)) is passed as the 2nd positional argument, so Fiber v3 runs it after the handler and it never executes._

**Endpoint-specific errors**
- 400: `Request could not be completed. Please try again.` - JSON bind fails
- 400: `<FormatValidationError text>` - validate-tag failure
- 400: `Your country cannot be changed once it has been set. Contact support if it is wrong` - ErrCountryLocked
- 400: `<ProfileValidationError text>` - bio / country / timezone rule
- 500: `Request could not be completed. Please try again.` - solver lookup fails, DOB invalid, or DB update fails (SolverErrorResponse: {success:false, error:string, data:null})

**Side effects:** UPDATE solvers with the changed columns (spoken_languages stored as JSON); purges the tz:<user_id> timezone cache.

**Request fields**

**Response 200 fields** `{success:true, data:{content:[ContentListItem], pagination:{page,limit,total}}}`
| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | |
| solver_id | uuid | |
| solver_name | string | `first_name + ' ' + last_name`, or 'Solver' when there is no solvers row |
| content_type | string | reel, video, blog, link, pdf, image, github_repo, code_snippet, resource, podcast |
| format | string | practical_demo, 2d_animation, 3d_animation, slide_based |
| title | string | |

| tags | string[], omitempty | |

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | owner, draft | 200 | ok |
| 2 | anonymous, draft | 404 | `content not found` (CONTENT_NOT_FOUND) |

Confirmed: the owner (Bearer) sees the draft; the same id without a token → 404 `CONTENT_NOT_FOUND`.

---

Returns one content item's full detail. This is the only single-item read the solver has: there is no `GET /solver/content/:id`. When the caller is the owner it returns the item in ANY status (draft, hidden, taken_down), skips the premium and free-preview gates, and includes the blog `body` and embed links. Use it to pre-fill the edit form with fields the list does not carry (description, body, html_embed_url, excalidraw_url, content_url, transcript_url).

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
`public.Use(RateLimitGlobal(RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR, default 1000/h per IP))` → `publicContent.Use(OptionalAuthMiddleware)`. The Bearer token is honoured for native clients (`X-App-Platform` ios/android). A bad, expired or revoked token falls through as ANONYMOUS without an error, and the owner then gets 404 on a draft. Send a valid token.

**Handler:** `content_handler.go:501` (GetContentDetail) → `content_service.go:2192` (GetContentDetailPublic → loadContentForViewer `:512` → authorizeContentAccess `:390` (the owner always passes) → getContentDetail `:2077`).

**Request fields**
Path `content_id` (UUID).

**Response 200 fields** `{success:true, data:{content:PublicContentDTO, solver:ContentSolverInfo, is_saved:bool, is_liked:bool}}`

The `content` object has these fields:
- id, solver_id (uuid; zeroed for anonymous posts, but not for the owner)
- content_type, format, title (string)
- description (string, omitempty)
- category (string, skill), sub_category (string, omitempty, focus area)
- tags (string[])
- labels, keywords, hashtags (string[], omitempty)
- is_anonymous (bool), podcast_type (omitempty), custom_category (omitempty)
- category_locked (bool): set true on publish, informational only (UpdateContent no longer enforces it)
- is_featured (bool)
- content_url (omitempty, link/github_repo)
- media_url, thumbnail_url, transcript_url (omitempty, presigned R2 URLs)
- duration (int, omitempty, seconds)
- status (string)
- is_synap_official, is_premium (bool)
- view_count, like_count, comment_count, share_count (int)
- body, html_embed_url, excalidraw_url (omitempty, blog only, from content_blog_details)
- published_at (omitempty), created_at, updated_at (RFC3339)

The `solver` object has: solver_id, first_name?, last_name?, pseudo_name?, avatar_url? (presigned), rating (float), is_verified (bool).

**Errors** (body `{success:false,error,error_code}`)
- 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid content ID"}`
- 404 `content not found` / CONTENT_NOT_FOUND: no row; a non-published row and the caller is not the owner; or a non-owner viewing an author who no longer passes the publish gate
- 410 `content has been deleted` / CONTENT_DELETED
- Non-owner only: 402 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED_ANONYMOUS / SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED_NO_ACTIVE / SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED_EXPIRED / PREVIEW_EXHAUSTED; 401 SIGN_IN_REQUIRED; 403 KYC_REQUIRED; 503 SUBSCRIPTION_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE / PREVIEW_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE
- 429 `{success:false,error:"Too many requests. Please try again later.",retry_after}`
- 500 `Failed to get content` / INTERNAL_ERROR

**Side effects**
Owner: none (no view is recorded for the owner). Non-owner: records the first view, may credit view earnings, a streak, and a WS view-count push to the solver.

**Mobile notes**
The detail is served from a cache that every write path invalidates after commit, so re-fetch after saving. Presigned URLs expire, so do not persist them.

**Unresolved**
None.

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy path | 200 | `Content updated successfully` |
| 2 | skill pair not verified | 400 | `choose a skill and focus area you are verified in` (SKILL_NOT_VERIFIED) |
| 3 | premium on a link | 400 | `Only 3D animated reels and videos can be marked as Premium` (PREMIUM_NOT_ALLOWED) |
| 4 | unknown id | 404 | `content not found` (CONTENT_NOT_FOUND) |
| 5 | edit while published | 200 | `Content updated successfully` |
| 6 | empty title | 400 | `Validation failed: title must be at least 3 characters` (VALIDATION_FAILED) |
| 7 | whitespace-only title | 400 | `title must be at least 3 characters` (VALIDATION_FAILED) |
| 8 | tag shorter than 2 | 400 | `Validation failed: tags[1] must be at least 2 characters` (VALIDATION_FAILED) |
| 9 | description over 5000 | 400 | `Validation failed: description must be at most 5000 characters` (VALIDATION_FAILED) |
| 10 | invalid content_url | 400 | `Validation failed: content_url must be a valid URL` (VALIDATION_FAILED) |

Confirmed (fixed 2026-10-25): empty or whitespace-only title → 400 `title must be at least 3 characters`; tag under 2 chars, description over 5000, or an invalid `content_url` → 400 `Validation failed: …` (VALIDATION_FAILED). Editing while published is allowed.

---

The main edit endpoint. It is a partial update: a field that is omitted or null is left unchanged. It uses POST, not PUT or PATCH. It never changes `status` (use publish or unpublish) and never changes media (use `/upload/:kind`). A published item stays published after an edit, and a draft stays a draft.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireFeatureAccess("content"). The route is `Post("/:content_id", contentWriteRL, UpdateContent)`, so the limiter sits in the HANDLER slot. Fiber v3 runs UpdateContent first, and the handler never calls Next, so **the 20/min write limiter never runs (dead)**.

**Handler:** `content_handler.go:280` (UpdateContent) → `content_service.go:1385` → `postgres/content_repository.go:293` (UpdateContent) and `:93` (UpsertBlogDetails for blogs).

**Request fields** (all optional; send only what changed). Since 2026-10-25 the handler validates the body like create does: a failing field → 400 `{success:false, error:"Validation failed: <field> ...", error_code:"VALIDATION_FAILED"}`.
| name | type | rule actually applied |
|---|---|---|
| title | string | 3–200 characters, and still ≥ 3 after trimming/control-character removal (else 400 `title must be at least 3 characters` / VALIDATION_FAILED) |
| description | string | ≤ 5000; same normalisation |
| category | string | skill. If the skill or focus-area pair changes, it must match one of the solver's VERIFIED skill → focus-area pairs (case-insensitive) and is stored in canonical casing. Otherwise 400 SKILL_NOT_VERIFIED. Can be changed after publish (no lock) |
| sub_category | string | focus area, same rule. Sending only one of category/sub_category re-checks it against the stored other half. An unchanged pair is not re-checked |
| tags | string[] | ≤ 10 tags, each 2–50 characters. Replaces the stored tags. `[]` clears them, so always send the current tags (the list endpoint returns them) |
| content_url | string | must be a valid URL, ≤ 500 (validator). Applied only when content_type is `link` or `github_repo`; ignored for other types |
| duration | int (seconds) | ignored for `podcast` (measured from the recording); no range check here (publish enforces it) |
| is_premium | bool | upgrading to true is allowed only for content_type reel or video with format `3d_animation`. Otherwise 400 PREMIUM_NOT_ALLOWED. Downgrading is always allowed |
| body | string | blog only. An explicit value overwrites the stored body; an empty string becomes NULL. Stored as-is (HTML) |
| html_embed_url | string | blog only; same pointer semantics |
| excalidraw_url | string | blog only; same pointer semantics |

Ignored if sent: status, media_url, thumbnail_url, transcript_url, format, content_type, is_anonymous, labels, keywords, hashtags, podcast_type, custom_category (these are not on the DTO, so they cannot be edited).

**Response 200 fields**
`{success:true, message:"Content updated successfully"}`. The updated object is NOT returned; re-fetch it.

**Errors** (`{success:false,error,error_code}`)
- 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid content ID"}`
- 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid request format"}` (bad JSON or wrong types)
- 400 `Validation failed: ...` / VALIDATION_FAILED (field rules above)
- 400 `title must be at least 3 characters` / VALIDATION_FAILED (blank or whitespace-only title)
- 400 `choose a skill and focus area you are verified in` / SKILL_NOT_VERIFIED
- 400 `Only 3D animated reels and videos can be marked as Premium` / PREMIUM_NOT_ALLOWED
- 403 `you do not own this content` / NOT_CONTENT_OWNER
- 404 `content not found` / CONTENT_NOT_FOUND
- 409 `this content is part of your skill verification and is awaiting admin review` / CONTENT_UNDER_VERIFICATION_REVIEW
- 410 `content has been deleted` / CONTENT_DELETED
- 410 `content has been taken down and cannot be republished` / CONTENT_TAKEN_DOWN (also raised when an admin takedown races the update)
- 500 `Failed to update content` / INTERNAL_ERROR (including a failed verified-skills lookup)
- plus the auth, role and feature-restriction 401/403 shapes described on the list endpoint

**Side effects**
UPDATE content: rewrites the full row from the loaded struct, including title, description, category, sub_category, tags, content_url, duration, is_premium and updated_at. On a published row with an admin category_lock_override set, the override is cleared. For a blog with body or embed fields, UPSERT content_blog_details runs in the same transaction. A `content.updated` event goes to the outbox/NATS (the consumer only logs it; there is no WS push). Detail, list and search caches are invalidated after commit.

**Mobile notes**
Load the item with GET /public/content/:id and the list first, send only the changed fields (always include tags if you send tags), then re-fetch. Mirror the same rules client-side (title 3–200, description ≤5000, tags ≤10 × 2–50) for instant feedback; the server enforces them too.

**Unresolved**
None.

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy path | 201 | ok |
| 2 | media on a link item | 400 | `upload rejected: link content takes a link, not a file upload` (INVALID_UPLOAD) |
| 3 | unknown kind | 400 | `kind must be media, thumbnail, or transcript` |

---

Uploads a file into one slot of the content row (media_url, thumbnail_url or transcript_url) and stores the R2 key. Uploading over an existing file REPLACES it. The old key stays in place until the new object is stored, so a failed replacement keeps the working file. This is the only way to set media; no endpoint accepts a URL or a key.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireFeatureAccess("content"). `contentUploadRL` (6/min) is in the handler slot, so it is **dead** (never runs). Fiber's global BodyLimit is 5.5GB.

**Handler:** `content_handler.go:924` (UploadContentFile) → `content_service.go:2675` (UploadContentMedia). Validation: `ValidateContentFile` `:1057`, `validateAuxiliaryUpload` `:1074`, `checkUploadSignature` `:1094`. R2 key: `content/{solverID}/{contentID}/{kind}-{safeFilename}` (`infra/storage/storage_service.go:174`).

**Request fields**
- `:kind` must be one of these values. Any other value returns 400 `kind must be media, thumbnail, or transcript`.
- Edge check on the Content-Length header: media > 5.5GB, thumbnail > 6MB or transcript > 3MB returns 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE.
- **thumbnail** (any content type): .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif, ≤ 5MB, and the bytes must sniff as image/*.
- **transcript** (any content type): .vtt .srt .txt, ≤ 2MB. This only fills `transcript_url`. Publish checks the content_transcripts row written by `POST /:id/transcript`, and transcripts are currently optional.
- **media**, by content_type:
  - video and reel: .mp4 .webm .mov, ≤ 5GB
  - blog: .md .txt .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif .svg .excalidraw, ≤ 10MB (diagram or attachment; the article text lives in `body`)
  - image: .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif .svg .excalidraw, ≤ 10MB
  - resource: .pdf .md .txt .zip, ≤ 100MB
  - code_snippet: .txt .md .js .ts .py .go .java .c .cpp .rs .rb .sh, ≤ 5MB
  - podcast: always rejected (its media is the session recording)
  - pdf and slide: rejected (retired)
  - link and github_repo: rejected (no file slot)
- Every upload: if the first 512 bytes sniff as text/html it is rejected. .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.webp/.gif must sniff as image/*, .pdf as application/pdf and .zip as application/zip.
- The stored MIME type is derived on the server from the extension; the client's Content-Type is ignored.

**Response 201 fields**
`{success:true, data:{kind:string, key:string}}`. `key` is the raw R2 object key, not a URL.

**Errors**
- 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid content ID"}`
- 400 `{success:false,error:"kind must be media, thumbnail, or transcript"}`
- 400 `{success:false,error:"file is required (multipart field 'file')"}`
- 400 INVALID_UPLOAD `{success:false,error:"upload rejected: <reason>",error_code:"INVALID_UPLOAD"}`. Reasons include: `file type .exe is not allowed for video content`, `file exceeds maximum size of 10MB for blog content`, `link content takes a link, not a file upload`, `a podcast's media is its session recording and cannot be uploaded`, `PDF and PPT/slide content are no longer supported`, `file type .bmp is not allowed for a thumbnail`, `thumbnail exceeds maximum size of 5MB`, `HTML documents cannot be uploaded`, `file content does not match its .png extension`
- 403 NOT_CONTENT_OWNER
- 404 CONTENT_NOT_FOUND
- 409 CONTENT_UNDER_VERIFICATION_REVIEW
- 410 CONTENT_DELETED
- 413 `{success:false,error:"File exceeds maximum size",error_code:"FILE_TOO_LARGE"}`
- 500 `Failed to upload content file` / INTERNAL_ERROR (R2 failure or storage not configured)
- plus the auth, role and feature-restriction 401/403 shapes

**Side effects**
- Empty slot: the row is first set to `uploading:<uuid>`, then to the final key. On an R2 failure it is set to `failed:<uuid>`.
- For media on video/reel/podcast with no duration, ffprobe fills `duration` (best-effort).
- Caches are invalidated.
- No event or WS push. Unlike publish, it does NOT enqueue the HLS, thumbnail or virus-scan pipeline.
- A taken-down row is not rejected up front, but the repo UPDATE skips taken_down rows, so the R2 object is written and the key is never stored.

**Mobile notes**
After an upload, re-fetch the list or detail to get a presigned URL. A large video is one request (no chunking or resumable upload), so keep the connection alive and show progress.

**Unresolved**
None.

Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**. | # | Case | HTTP | Result | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | happy path | 201 | ok | | 2 | AVIF (allowlisted extension) | 400 | `invalid blog image: that file is not an image` (INVALID_UPLOAD) | | 3 | SVG | 400 | `invalid blog image: svg images are not supported here - use PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP or AVIF` (INVALID_UPLOAD) | **Confirmed defect:** an AVIF file → 400 `invalid blog image: that file is not an image` although `.avif` is allowlisted. SVG → 400. PNG → 201 with a root-relative `url`. --- Uploads one picture to place between paragraphs of a blog body. It is not tied to a content id; the authenticated solver is the only authorisation. The returned `url` is root-relative and goes into the body HTML as ``, which is then saved through the update endpoint's `body` field. **Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs** AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireFeatureAccess("content") → **RateLimitContentUpload(30/min per IP), which works here** because the limiter is in the variadic slot and runs before the handler. **Handler:** `content_blog_image_handler.go:38` (UploadBlogInlineImage) → `usecases/content_blog_image_service.go:72`. R2 key: `content/blog-inline/{solverID}/{imageID}-{filename}`. The row goes in `content_blog_images`. **Request fields** - `file` (multipart): extension .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.avif. Size must be > 0 and ≤ 8MB, with an edge check of Content-Length ≤ 9MB. The first 512 bytes must sniff as image/*. The stored MIME type comes from the extension. **Response 201 fields** `{success:true, data:{id:uuid, url:string, mime_type:string, size_bytes:int}}`. `url` = `/api/v1/public/content/blog-images/{id}`, served without auth. **Errors** - 400 `{success:false,error:"file is required (multipart field 'file')"}` - 400 INVALID_UPLOAD `{success:false,error:"invalid blog image: ",error_code:"INVALID_UPLOAD"}`. Reasons: `svg images are not supported here - use PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP or AVIF`, `the file is empty`, `image exceeds maximum size of 8MB`, `that file is not an image` - 413 `{success:false,error:"Image exceeds maximum size of 8MB",error_code:"FILE_TOO_LARGE"}` - 429 `{success:false,error:"Too many requests. Please try again later.",retry_after}` - 500 `{success:false,error:"Failed to upload image",error_code:"INTERNAL_ERROR"}` - plus the auth, role and feature-restriction 401/403 shapes **Side effects** An R2 object is written, then a content_blog_images row. No event or push. **Mobile notes** Prefix the root-relative `url` with the API origin for in-app preview, but store it root-relative in the body. The image GET needs no auth and is cached as immutable. **Known defect (AVIF):** `.avif` is on the extension allowlist, but the byte check uses Go 1.25 `http.DetectContentType`, which has no AVIF signature (an `ftyp avif` file sniffs as `application/octet-stream`). Real AVIF uploads therefore fail with 400 `that file is not an image`. Until fixed, the app should convert to WEBP/JPG before upload. **Unresolved** Whether Go's http.DetectContentType recognises AVIF bytes as image/* was not verified. If it does not, .avif uploads always fail with `that file is not an image`.

Call once per language. The publish gate (if a type were made to require transcripts again) reads any one row, using LIMIT 1 regardless of language.

Returns the same verdict that `POST /:id/publish` enforces, so the app can show a banner or disable the Publish button. Publishing needs skill verification `verified` AND KYC verification_level `full`.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireFeatureAccess("content"). No limiter. It is registered before `/:content_id`, so the literal path wins.

**Handler:** `content_handler.go:1024` (GetPublishEligibility) → `content_service.go:1566`.

**Request fields**
None.

**Response 200 fields** `{success:true, data:{...}}`
| field | type | meaning |

Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy path | 200 | `Content published successfully` |
| 2 | already published | 409 | `content is already published` (ALREADY_PUBLISHED) |
| 3 | publish deleted item | 410 | `content has been deleted` (CONTENT_DELETED) |

Confirmed: already published → 409; a row whose title is blank (only possible for rows saved before 2026-10-25) → 400 `title must be at least 3 characters` instead of the old 500; deleted item → 410.

---

Moves a draft (or hidden) item to `published`. This is the single publish entry point.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireFeatureAccess("content"). `contentWriteRL` is in the handler slot, so it is **dead**.

**Handler:** `content_handler.go:310` (PublishContent) → `content_service.go:1644`.

**Request fields**
None (no body).

**Validation order**
1. Ownership, deleted, already published, taken_down, verification under review.
2. Title and category must not be empty.
3. Media present for video, reel and podcast. A blog may be text-only.
4. Duration ≥ 1s for video and podcast. If it is missing, ffprobe backfills it from R2.
5. A reel with a known duration must be 3–90s.
6. Publish gate (skill verified + KYC full).
7. R2 HeadObject on the media key (3s timeout).

The transcript is not required.

**Response 200 fields**
`{success:true, message:"Content published successfully", data:{content: Content}}`. `content` is the FULL internal `domain.Content`, not PublicContentDTO. It includes `category_lock_override`, `feature_priority`, `verification_id`, `verification_review_pending`, `source_recording_id` and `draft_expires_at` where set. `media_url`, `thumbnail_url` and `transcript_url` are RAW R2 keys, not presigned. `body` is absent (not hydrated). `status` is `published`, `category_locked` is true, and `published_at` is the current time.

**Errors** (`{success:false,error,error_code}`)
- 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid content ID"}`
- 400 MEDIA_REQUIRED `media upload is required before publishing this content type: video`
- 400 DURATION_INVALID `Content must be at least 1 second long (got 0)`. For a reel: `Content must be at least 1 second long (reels must be 90s or shorter, got 120s)` / `(reels must be at least 3s, got 2s)`
- 403 NOT_CONTENT_OWNER
- 403 SOLVER_NOT_VERIFIED `Solver must complete skill verification before publishing content` (also returned when the eligibility lookup fails)
- 403 SOLVER_KYC_INCOMPLETE `Solver must complete identity (KYC) verification before publishing content`
- 404 CONTENT_NOT_FOUND
- 409 ALREADY_PUBLISHED `content is already published`
- 409 CONTENT_UNDER_VERIFICATION_REVIEW
- 409 MEDIA_NOT_READY `Media upload is still in progress, please wait` (R2 object missing or probe error)
- 410 CONTENT_DELETED
- 410 CONTENT_TAKEN_DOWN `content has been taken down and cannot be republished`
- 400 `title must be at least 3 characters` / VALIDATION_FAILED: a row saved with a blank title before 2026-10-25 (updates can no longer blank it)
- 500 `{success:false,error:"Internal error, please try again",error_code:"INTERNAL"}` (unexpected failures, including an empty category)
- plus the auth, role and feature-restriction 401/403 shapes

**Side effects**
- In one transaction (SELECT … FOR UPDATE re-check): UPDATE status=published, category_locked=true, published_at=now, draft_expires_at=NULL, plus the outbox `content.published` event.
- After commit: virus-scan and probe jobs are enqueued. For video, reel and podcast, HLS transcode and WebP thumbnail jobs are also enqueued.
- The NATS consumer pushes a **WS event to the owner**: `{id, type:"content.published", user_id, data:{content_id, title, status:"published", published_at}, timestamp}`.
- It fans out `content.new_from_followed_solver` (data `{content_id, solver_id, ...}`) to every follower as a WS push plus an in-app notification.
- Caches are invalidated.

**Mobile notes**
Call publish-eligibility first. On MEDIA_NOT_READY, retry after a few seconds. Listen for the `content.published` WS event to flip the badge.

**Unresolved**
None.

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy path | 200 | `rating=0` |

---

The one READ endpoint for the pricing-tier screen. It returns the solver's saved rate (`price_per_minute`, `price_multiplier`), whether a rate above the base is available (`can_set_pricing`), and `tier_unlock_data`: the full tier ladder with per-tier lock state and progress against that tier's admin-configured thresholds. Only pricing/tier fields are documented here. The full profile carries many more fields (name, bio, avatar, KYC level, completion meter, etc.); see the Solver Profile folder.

No other solver endpoint returns tier data: `GET /solver/dashboard` has no price/tier fields, `GET /solver/score` returns a ranking-score breakdown with no price/tier fields, and there is **no solver-side tier/upgrade-request endpoint** (see Unresolved).

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**: group `.Use()` chain on `/solver`: `AuthMiddleware` (Bearer PASETO v4 access token), `RequireRole("solver")`, `tzMiddleware`. No per-route middleware.

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/solver_profile_handler.go:77` (GetProfile) → `Backend/internal/core/usecases/solver_profile_service.go:191` (GetProfile) → `buildTierUnlockData` at `solver_profile_service.go:453`, `evaluatePricing` at `solver_profile_service.go:352`. Route: `routes.go:783`.

**Request fields**: none.

**Response 200 fields** (envelope `{success, message, data}`; pricing-related fields of `data` only):
| field | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `price_per_minute` | number | Saved rate in ₹ per session minute (solvers.price_per_minute). Base is 5. |
| `price_multiplier` | number | Stored multiplier = price/5 (₹5=1, ₹10=2, ₹15=3, ₹20=4). |
| `can_set_pricing` | bool | Same value as `tier_unlock_data.canSetPricing` (true when maxUnlockedTier > 0). The DB column `can_set_pricing` is NOT used. |
| `completed_sessions` | int | Same counter the sessions threshold uses. |
| `rating`, `total_reviews` | number, int | Inputs to the useful-feedback % (see below). |
| `tier_unlock_data` | object, omitempty | Always set by GetProfile in practice. **Keys inside are camelCase.** |
| `tier_unlock_data.currentTier` | int | Index into `tiers` of the highest tier at or below the saved price. |
| `tier_unlock_data.maxUnlockedTier` | int | Highest index the solver may save now. Same check the POST uses. Clamp the slider to it. |
| `tier_unlock_data.canSetPricing` | bool | `maxUnlockedTier > 0`. |
| `tier_unlock_data.lockReason` | string, omitempty | Why the first locked tier is locked, e.g. `To unlock ₹10/min you need 400 completed sessions (you have 12), 50 unique seekers (you have 4), 80% useful feedback (you have 72%).` Omitted when every tier is unlocked. When evaluation fails: `Higher rates are unavailable right now. Please try again later.` |
| `tier_unlock_data.tiers[]` | array | Cheapest first: the ₹5 base plus every ACTIVE row of `solver_pricing_unlock_rules` priced above 5. If the solver holds a rate whose rule was deactivated, that rate also appears as a rung with no `progress`. |
| `tiers[].price` | number | ₹/min. Send this exact value to POST /solver/profile/pricing. |
| `tiers[].multiplier` | number | price / 5 (float). |
| `tiers[].unlocked` | bool | `index <= maxUnlockedTier`. |
| `tiers[].progress` | object, omitempty | Missing on the base tier (and on a retained rule-less rung). |
| `progress.sessions` | `{current:int, required:int}` | current = solvers.completed_sessions. |
| `progress.uniqueSeekers` | `{current:int, required:int}` | current = COUNT(DISTINCT seeker_id) over the solver's bookings with booking_status='completed'. |
| `progress.usefulFeedback` | `{current:number, required:number}` | Percent 0-100. current = (rating/5)*100 if total_reviews > 0, else 0. No per-review "useful" flag exists, so this is derived from the average rating. |

Unlock rule: tier N is unlocked only if the solver meets every threshold of tier N **and of every tier below it** (evaluation stops at the first unmet tier). A required value of 0 counts as met.

Seeded defaults in `schema.sql:4150`. Admins can change them at runtime via `/admin/solver-pricing-rules`:
| price | sessions | unique seekers | feedback % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10 | 400 | 50 | 80 |
| 15 | 800 | 100 | 85 |
| 20 | 1200 | 200 | 90 |
The client must not hard-code these. Build the slider from `tiers`.

**Errors** (body `{success:false, error, data:null}` from the handler; middleware bodies have no `data` key):
- 401 `Authentication required`: no token (AuthMiddleware) or missing role local.
- 401 `Invalid or expired token`: bad or expired access token.
- 401 `Session has been revoked. Please login again` / `Session has been revoked or client identity mismatch. Please login again`.
- 401 `Request could not be completed. Please try again.` (handler, user_id missing from context).
- 403 `You do not have permission to access this resource`: role is not solver.
- 500 `Request could not be completed. Please try again.`: solver row not found or DB error.

**Side effects**: none. Read only. The solver row comes from the Ristretto cache key `solver:profile:<user_id>` (TTL 5 min). `completed_sessions` and `rating` can therefore lag up to 5 min unless something invalidates the cache. Pricing rules and the unique-seeker count are read uncached on every call.

**Mobile notes**: Call this on screen open, and call it again after every successful POST /solver/profile/pricing (the POST returns no data). Build the slider/cards from `tier_unlock_data.tiers`, select `currentTier`, disable indexes above `maxUnlockedTier`, and show `lockReason` under the slider. No WS event fires when tiers change, so re-fetch on screen focus.

**Unresolved**: (1) `solver_upgrade_requests` (admin `GET /admin/solver-upgrade-requests`, approve/reject) is a different system. It sets `solver_levels.level_name` (basic/intermediate/advanced/expert) and has nothing to do with price tiers. No code anywhere INSERTs into `solver_upgrade_requests`, and there is no solver-side create/status endpoint. Price tiers unlock automatically from the thresholds; there is nothing to request. (2) The user ID→solver mapping relies on solvers.id = users.id (GetSolverByUserID queries `WHERE id = $1`).

Confirmed. ---

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**: group `.Use()` chain: `AuthMiddleware`, `RequireRole("solver")`, `tzMiddleware`. The route is `solver.Post("/profile/pricing", solverProfileRestrict, solverProfileHandler.UpdatePricing)`. Because of the Fiber v3 ordering trap, `UpdatePricing` runs and responds first, so `RequireFeatureAccess("profile_edit")` never runs. **An admin `profile_edit` feature restriction does NOT block this endpoint.**

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/solver_profile_handler.go:312` → `Backend/internal/core/usecases/solver_profile_service.go:671` → `Backend/internal/adapter/db/postgres/solver_profile_repository.go:367` (via cache decorator `Backend/internal/adapter/cache/solver_profile_repository.go:147`). Route: `routes.go:780`.

**Request fields**:
| name | type | required | validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price_per_minute` | number | yes | `validate:"required,min=5"`. It must also exactly equal (float ==) one `tiers[].price` from GET /solver/profile. There is no upper bound in the DTO; the ladder is admin-configured. Send it as a JSON number, not a string. |

**Service logic** (in order):
1. Load the solver by user_id. On failure: 400 generic.
2. `price_per_minute == 5`: always allowed. Writes 5 / multiplier 1, no threshold check.
3. Build the ladder from active `solver_pricing_unlock_rules`. If evaluation errors, fail closed: 403 with the bare `ErrPricingUnlockNotMet` message.
4. The price is not a ladder rung: 400 `Price per minute must be one of the available pricing tiers`.
5. The requested index > max(maxUnlockedTier, currentTier): 403. The solver may always re-save the rate they already hold, or anything lower, even if an admin later raised its thresholds.
6. Otherwise write price + multiplier `int(price/5)`.

**Response 200 fields**: `success` (true), `message` (`Pricing updated successfully`). The `data` key is absent (nil + omitempty).

**Errors** (handler body `{success:false, error, data:null}`):
- 400 `Request could not be completed. Please try again.`: body is not valid JSON or a field has the wrong type (e.g. a string); validation failed (missing, 0, or < 5); solver not found; DB write failed.
- 400 `Price per minute must be one of the available pricing tiers`: value >= 5 that is not a ladder rung (e.g. 12, or a tier the admin deactivated that the solver does not hold).
- 403 `you have not met the platform credibility thresholds for this price tier: To unlock ₹<price>/min you need <list>.`: thresholds unmet. The `<list>` names the unmet thresholds of the **first locked tier**, which may be lower than the requested tier. Format: `400 completed sessions (you have 12), 50 unique seekers (you have 4), 80% useful feedback (you have 72%)`.
- 403 `you have not met the platform credibility thresholds for this price tier`: no suffix. The pricing evaluation itself failed (DB error); this fails closed.
- 401 / 403 from middleware: same bodies as GET /solver/profile (`{success:false, error}` with no `data`).

**Side effects**: `UPDATE solvers SET hourly_rate=$1, price_per_minute=$1, price_multiplier=$2, updated_at=NOW()`. Invalidates cache keys `solver:profile:<id>`, `solver:profile:id:<id>`, `public:solver:<id>`. No WS event, no push, no email, no notification, no audit row. Existing bookings keep their frozen `price_multiplier`/`minutes_deducted`. The new rate applies only to bookings created afterwards.

**Mobile notes**: Only offer prices from `tier_unlock_data.tiers` with `index <= maxUnlockedTier`. After a 200, re-fetch GET /solver/profile to refresh `price_per_minute`, `price_multiplier` and `currentTier`. Show a 403 `error` string verbatim; it tells the solver what is missing. Saving 5 always succeeds.

**Unresolved**: The stored `price_multiplier` is `int(price/5)`, so a non-multiple-of-5 tier (e.g. ₹12) truncates to 2. Booking ignores the stored multiplier anyway (see the seeker-facing entry).

A representative seeker-facing read of a solver's rate. Brief by design; see the Explore folder for the full profile. The price field is `price_per_minute` (₹/min, read from `solvers.hourly_rate`). **No multiplier is exposed here.** Explore search results (`TrendingSolver` / search items) use the same `price_per_minute` key.

**Response 200 fields (pricing-relevant)**: `data.price_per_minute` (number, ₹/min), plus `data.solver_id`, `data.level_name` (solver_levels name, default `basic`; this is NOT the price tier), `data.rating`, `data.completed_sessions`. The full object has more (skills, verified_skills, languages, projects, resolution_rate, ...).

**Errors**: 400 `{success:false,error:"Invalid solver ID"}` (not a UUID). 404 `{success:false,error:"Solver not found"}`, returned for any listability miss: not active, not verified, role-switched, skill verification not verified, or KYC light/standard/full not all verified.

**How seeker wallet minutes derive from the tier** (`Backend/internal/core/usecases/booking_service.go:1337-1372`, CreateBooking):
- `solverPrice` = `solvers.price_per_minute`, clamped to a minimum of 1. Above ₹100 the booking is rejected.
- `priceMultiplier = solverPrice / base_minute_value`. `base_minute_value` is admin platform_settings `pricing.base_minute_value` (default ₹5; the same value withdrawals pay at), floored at 1. **The stored `solvers.price_multiplier` is NOT used for charging.**
- `minutes_deducted (per seat) = ceil(duration_minutes × priceMultiplier)`. For `booking_type = anonymous` this is then multiplied by `booking.anonymous_minutes_multiplier` (default ×2) and ceil'd again. A group `pay_all` booking multiplies by group_size.
- Extensions: `ceil(extra_minutes × booking.price_multiplier)` (× anonymous multiplier when anonymous), using the multiplier frozen on the booking (`booking_service.go:3993`).
- Example with base 5: a ₹10 tier is 2 wallet minutes per session minute, so a 30-min session debits 60 minutes. A ₹15 tier gives 3×, ₹20 gives 4×.
- The booking response carries `minutes_deducted`, `price_multiplier` and `solver_price`.

**Mobile notes**: The seeker UI must show minutes, never ₹. Display `price_per_minute / 5` as "N minutes per minute" only as an estimate. The authoritative number is `minutes_deducted` from the booking create/quote response. `base_minute_value` is not exposed to seekers by any endpoint (the solver-only `GET /solver/settings/country` exposes it as `base_rate_inr`).

**Unresolved**: If an admin sets `pricing.base_minute_value` to anything other than 5, the solver profile's `price_multiplier`/`tiers[].multiplier` (always price/5) no longer match what seekers are charged.

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | validation: below min 10 | 400 | `Invalid extension parameters` |
| 2 | anon session, 4 min left | 200 | `status="pending_approval"`, `minutes_reserved=30` |
| 3 | second request while one is pending | 400 | `an extension request is already pending for this session` |
| 4 | anon, 20 min → expect 20×1×3 frozen (wallet before 420) | 200 | `status="pending_approval"`, `minutes_reserved=60` |
| 5 | new request after a decline (wallet before 420) | 200 | `status="pending_approval"`, `minutes_reserved=30` |
| 6 | request then let it expire (wallet before 420) | 200 | `status="pending_approval"`, `minutes_reserved=30` |
| 7 | WebSocket frames both apps received during the decline + expiry runs | 200 | ok |

Confirmed on an anonymous session: +10 min reserved 30 minutes, +20 min reserved 60 (×3 anonymous multiplier). A second request while one is pending → 400; outside the last 5 minutes → 409 `extension_too_early`. The last row lists the WebSocket frames both apps received: `extension_requested` (solver), `extension.declined` and **`extension.expired`** (seeker and solver). Note: `session_extension_requests.frozen_minutes` is stored as 0 (the refund still uses the right amount).

---

The seeker asks for more time on a live session. The server creates a `session_extension_requests` row with status `pending` and an approval window (env `EXTENSION_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default and current .env value 120s). It holds (freezes) the wallet minutes and pushes `extension_requested` to the solver. Nothing is added to the session until the solver approves.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
`seeker` group `.Use()`: AuthMiddleware (Bearer token for native clients) → RequireRole(seeker) → tz middleware → RequireNoVerificationLock → RequireCompleteProfile. The profile gate allows `/api/v1/seeker/sessions/*` but explicitly BLOCKS `/sessions/:id/extend` (regex `profileGateSessionPurchase`), so a seeker with an incomplete profile gets 403 PROFILE_INCOMPLETE. No verification-level middleware. `bookingRateLimiter` sits in the Fiber v3 handler slot (`Post(path, bookingRateLimiter, ExtendSession)`), so ExtendSession runs first and the limiter never runs (dead).

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/booking_handler.go:1497`. Service: `Backend/internal/core/usecases/booking_service.go:3402`.

**Request fields**
| name | type | required | validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| extra_minutes | int | yes | `required,min=10,max=60` |

**Service rules (in order)**
1. The session must belong to the caller (else 403) and have status `active`.
2. Window: the request is allowed only when `scheduled_start + duration + extended_minutes - now <= 5 min` (`extensionWindowOpen`). Otherwise 409 `extension_too_early`.
3. Cap: `booking.duration + max(extended_minutes, sum approved) + extra <= MAX_SESSION_MINUTES_TOTAL` (env, default 240).
4. Pre-flight overlap probes for the solver's and the seeker's next booking (they fail open on DB error): 409 `solver_unavailable_for_extension` / `seeker_busy_for_extension`. No minutes are frozen.
5. If a still-unexpired `pending` request exists → 400 already pending.
6. Create the request row, then freeze `extensionFreezeMinutes` = `ceil(extra_minutes × booking.price_multiplier)`. **Anonymous bookings:** that value is then multiplied again by `ceil(× booking.anonymous_minutes_multiplier)` (platform setting, default 2). Idempotency key `freeze-<booking_id>-ext-<request_id>`. If the freeze fails, the row is marked `declined`.

**Response 200 fields** (`data` = `domain.ExtendSessionResponse`)
| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| request_id | uuid | extension request id |
| new_duration_minutes | int | PROSPECTIVE total once approved (booking duration + extensions so far + this request) |
| minutes_reserved | int, omitempty | wallet minutes frozen (multipliers included) |
| remaining_seconds | int | the approval window in seconds (120 by default). Size the UI countdown from this value. |
| status | string | always `pending_approval` here |
| new_end_time_utc, seeker_timezone, seeker_local_end_time, solver_timezone, solver_local_end_time | omitempty | NOT set on this endpoint (only on approve) |

**Errors** (body `{success:false, error}` plus `code` where shown)
- 401 `Authentication required` (also the token errors from AuthMiddleware)
- 403 `You do not have permission to access this resource` (role is not seeker)
- 403 PROFILE_INCOMPLETE (profile gate) / 403 VERIFICATION_LOCKED (custom-link KYC grace lock)
- 400 `Invalid session ID` / `Invalid request format` / `Invalid extension parameters` (extra_minutes outside 10–60 or missing)
- 404 `Session not found`
- 403 `You are not authorized to perform this action` (not your session)
- 400 `can only extend active sessions`
- 400 `failed to retrieve booking for extension`
- 409 code `extension_too_early`
- 400 `total session time cannot exceed 240 minutes`
- 409 code `solver_unavailable_for_extension` / `seeker_busy_for_extension`
- 400 `an extension request is already pending for this session`
- 400 `insufficient Synap Minutes balance for extension`
- 400 `failed to reserve balance for extension`
- 400 `Failed to extend session` (generic internal error)

**Side effects**
- Inserts a `session_extension_requests` row (pending, expires_at = now + window).
- Wallet freeze of `minutes_reserved` with reason `Session extension requested (+N min) — minutes held`.
- An in-process timer plus the 20s sweeper settle the request as `expired` after the window, refund the hold, and push WS `extension.expired` to BOTH the seeker and the solver: data `{request_id, session_id, extra_minutes, message:"Extension request expired. Your minutes have been returned."}` (envelope `{id, type, user_id, data, timestamp}`).
- Outbox event `booking.extension_requested` → NATS → WS frame to the **solver**: `type: "extension_requested"`, data `{request_id, session_id, seeker_id, extra_minutes, expires_at, timeout_seconds, message:"Session extension requested. Please accept or reject."}`. The WS envelope is `{id, type, user_id, data, timestamp}`.

**Receiving the WS events in the app:** open `wss://<host>/api/v1/ws` (`ws://` in dev) with headers `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` and `X-App-Platform: ios|android`, and no `Origin` header. Native clients without an Origin are accepted since 2026-10-25; before that the upgrade was rejected with 500. Every frame is `{id, type, user_id, data, timestamp}`; the extension types are `extension_requested` (solver), `extension.approved`, `extension.declined`, `extension.expired` (both). The first frame is plain JSON `{type:"encryption_key", key:<base64 32-byte key>}`; every later frame is base64(12-byte nonce ‖ AES-256-GCM ciphertext) of that JSON envelope — decrypt with the key from the first frame.

**Money: charge and refund**
- The frozen hold is the charge for an approved extension. Approval does no further wallet write; the hold is consumed at session end.
- Decline, expiry, or an approval the DB rejects (overlap) refunds exactly the same `extensionFreezeMinutes` value. The refund goes through `settleExtensionRequest` under ONE idempotency key per request, `refund-<booking_id>-ext-<request_id>`, so a request is never refunded twice.
- The refund runs in the same transaction as the conditional pending→terminal status write.

**Mobile notes**
- Show the Extend button only in the last 5 minutes of the session (server enforces this).
- Preview the cost as `ceil(ceil(extra × price_multiplier) × anon_mult)` for anonymous bookings and `ceil(extra × price_multiplier)` otherwise. `price_multiplier` comes from GET /seeker/bookings/:booking_id; `anon_mult` comes from GET /public/booking-config.
- After the request, listen for WS `extension.approved` / `extension.declined` / **`extension.expired`** (since 2026-10-25). Poll GET /seeker/bookings/:booking_id (`extension_status`, `extension_remaining_seconds`) only as a fallback when the socket was down.

**Unresolved**
- RequireNoVerificationLock lets a locked seeker through only when the path contains their graced BOOKING id. This route carries the SESSION id, so a seeker inside a custom-link KYC grace window probably gets 403 VERIFICATION_LOCKED here, unless session id equals booking id (unverified).

### Live test 2026-10-25
Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | body {} without approve (request pending) | 400 | `approve is required: true to approve the extension, false to decline it` |
| 2 | happy path | 200 | `status="approved"` |
| 3 | nothing pending any more | 400 | `no pending extension request found` |
| 4 | approve after expiry | 400 | `no pending extension request found` |

Confirmed. **`approve` is now required:** a body of `{}` → 400 and the request stays pending (the timer still shows it). Approving after the 120 s window returns 400 `no pending extension request found` (the sweeper has already settled it as `expired`).

---

The solver approves the session's newest pending extension request. The pending→approved claim and `sessions.extended_minutes += extra` run in ONE transaction. The auto-end timer is rescheduled to the new end, and both parties get `extension.approved`.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
`solver` group: AuthMiddleware → RequireRole(solver) → tz. Then `solverSessionExt.Use(RequireVerification("standard"))` runs, because this route is registered after that Use. `bookingRateLimiter` is in the handler slot, so it is dead.

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/booking_handler.go:1751`. Service: `Backend/internal/core/usecases/booking_service.go:3575`.

**Request fields**
| name | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| approve | bool | **yes** | `true` = approve, `false` = decline. Missing → 400 `approve is required: true to approve the extension, false to decline it` (since 2026-10-25; it used to decline silently). |

**Response 200 fields** (`data` = ExtendSessionResponse)
| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| request_id | uuid | |
| new_duration_minutes | int | booking.duration_minutes + total extended minutes after this approval |
| remaining_seconds | int | seconds until the new end (scheduled_start + new_duration), floored at 0 |
| status | string | `approved` |
| new_end_time_utc | RFC3339 UTC | |
| seeker_timezone / seeker_local_end_time | string / RFC3339 with offset, omitempty | new end in the seeker's profile tz |
| solver_timezone / solver_local_end_time | string / RFC3339 with offset, omitempty | new end in the solver's profile tz |
| minutes_reserved | omitted | 0 on this path |

**Errors** (`{success:false,error}` plus `code`)
- 401 `Authentication required`; 403 verification body (see responses); 403 role
- 400 `Invalid session ID` / `Invalid request format` (malformed JSON)
- 400 `approve is required: true to approve the extension, false to decline it` (no `approve` key)
- 404 `Session not found`; 403 `You are not authorized to perform this action` (not the assigned solver)
- 400 `no pending extension request found`
- 400 `extension request has expired`. Side effect: the request is settled `expired` and the seeker is refunded.
- 400 `extension request is no longer pending`, when a race was lost to decline, expiry, or a double click
- 409 code `extension_conflict`, solver's next booking overlaps: `Unable to approve extension - you have another session scheduled right after this one, so it can't be extended without overlapping your next booking.`
- 409 code `extension_conflict`, seeker's next booking overlaps: `Unable to approve extension - the seeker has another session scheduled right after this one, so it can't run any longer.` On both 409s the request is closed as `declined` and the hold is refunded (`refund-<booking>-ext-<request>`).
- 400 `Failed to process extension request` (generic)

**Side effects**
- `session_extension_requests.status = approved`; `sessions.extended_minutes` increases.
- The auto-end goroutine is rescheduled for the new end.
- The frozen hold stays in place and is consumed at session end. There is no extra debit here.
- Outbox `extension.approved` → WS frame `type: "extension.approved"` to BOTH the seeker and the solver, data `{request_id, session_id, extra_minutes, new_duration_minutes, remaining_time_seconds, new_end_time_utc, message:"Extension approved."}`.

**Mobile notes**
- Get the request to approve from the WS `extension_requested` frame. If the socket missed it, read `pending_extension` on GET /solver/sessions/:id/timer.
- The server keeps no request id in the call: it always acts on the newest pending row.
- Re-sync the countdown from `remaining_seconds` or the WS frame. The LiveKit token may need refreshing for the longer session.

| 2 | empty body {} — approve omitted | 400 | `approve is required: true to approve the extension, false to decline it` |
| 3 | explicit decline of that request | 200 | `status="declined"` |

Confirmed: decline refunds the hold in full. `{}` → 400 (no longer a silent decline); `{"approve": false}` declines. The decline response carries `new_duration_minutes: 0`.

---

This is the same endpoint as approve, called with `approve:false` (or with the field missing). The newest pending request is settled as `declined`, and the seeker's hold is refunded in the same transaction.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
Same as approve: Auth → RequireRole(solver) → tz → RequireVerification(standard). The rate limiter is dead (handler slot).

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/booking_handler.go:1751`. Service: `booking_service.go:3575` (decline branch). Settlement: `settleExtensionRequest` at `booking_service.go:3900`.

**Request fields**
| name | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| approve | bool | **yes** | send `false` to decline. Omitting it → 400 (since 2026-10-25) |

**Response 200 fields**
| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| request_id | uuid | |
| new_duration_minutes | int | always 0 here (field is not omitempty) |
| remaining_seconds | int | always 0 here |
| status | string | `declined` |

**Errors**
- 400 `no pending extension request found`, 400 `extension request has expired` (settled as expired and refunded), 400 `extension request is no longer pending` (lost a race)
- 400 `something went wrong, please try again` is replaced by the default `Failed to process extension request` when the refund transaction fails. The request then stays pending and the expiry path refunds it.
- 401 / 403 / 404 as for approve

**Side effects**
- status → `declined`. The wallet is unfrozen for `extensionFreezeMinutes` (anonymous multiplier included) under key `refund-<booking_id>-ext-<request_id>`, reason `Session extension declined (+N min) — held minutes returned`.
- Outbox `extension.declined` → WS frame `type: "extension.declined"` to BOTH the seeker and the solver, data `{request_id, session_id, extra_minutes, message:"Extension declined."}`.

**Mobile notes**
- Always send `approve`; a body without it is rejected with 400 instead of being treated as a decline.

Run against the dev API (:8081) with throwaway seeker/solver accounts (deleted afterwards, R2 files removed). Each call below is saved as an example marked **(live 2026-10-25)**.

| # | Case | HTTP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | happy path | 200 | `status="in_progress"`, `minutes_deducted=60`, `extension_status="pending"` |
| 2 | while the request is pending | 200 | `status="in_progress"`, `minutes_deducted=60`, `extension_status="pending"` |
| 3 | after decline | 200 | `status="in_progress"`, `minutes_deducted=60`, `extension_status="declined"` |
| 4 | after expiry — wallet before 420, frozen 390, now 420 | 200 | `status="in_progress"`, `minutes_deducted=60`, `extension_status="expired"` |

Confirmed `extension_status` values: `pending` (with `extension_remaining_seconds` counting down from ~120), `approved`, `declined`, `expired`. Expiry refunds the hold. Since 2026-10-25 expiry is also pushed as WS `extension.expired`, so this poll is only a fallback.

---

There is no dedicated extension status or cancel endpoint. The seeker reads the state of its newest extension request from the booking-detail response. Only the extension-related fields are documented here; the full booking-detail payload belongs to the bookings spec.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
seeker group (Auth → RequireRole(seeker) → tz → RequireNoVerificationLock → RequireCompleteProfile; GET `/seeker/bookings/:id` is allowed) → `bookings.Use(RequireFeatureAccess("booking"))`. `requireLight` is in the handler slot (`Get("/:booking_id", requireLight, GetBookingDetail)`), so it never runs.

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/booking_handler.go:269`. Extension block: `Backend/internal/core/usecases/booking_service.go:~710-735` (repo `GetLatestExtensionRequest`, `booking_repository.go:2073`).

**Response 200 fields (extension subset)**
| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| session_id | uuid, omitempty | |
| session_status | string, omitempty | |
| price_multiplier | float | used to preview extension cost |
| extension_status | string, omitempty | newest request: `pending`, `approved`, `declined`, `expired`. A `pending` row past `expires_at` is reported as `expired`. Absent if no request was ever made. |
| extension_remaining_seconds | int, omitempty | approval window left (0 unless pending) |
| extension_extra_minutes | int, omitempty | minutes asked for |

**Errors**
- 401 `Authentication required`; 400 `Invalid booking ID`; 404 `Booking not found`; 403 `You are not authorized to perform this action`
- 403 feature-restricted body (`restricted:true, feature:"booking"`)

**Side effects:** none.

**Mobile notes**
- Poll while waiting (the web uses 5s) as a fallback for missed WS `extension.approved` / `extension.declined` frames. Expiry has no WS frame, so the poll is the only expiry signal.
- A request cannot be withdrawn by the seeker. It ends only by approve, decline, expiry, or session end; session end closes it as `expired` and refunds.

**Changed 2026-10-25:** when a request lapses the server now pushes WS `extension.expired` to both sides (data `{request_id, session_id, extra_minutes, message}`), so this read is only a fallback for a missed socket frame.

A public, unauthenticated config snapshot that clients use for cost previews and session-UI flags. **No server-side cost preview or estimate endpoint exists.** Routes, the explore handlers and the booking handlers were searched for preview/estimate/cost/quote. The web SeekerExplore computes the anonymous cost client-side from this multiplier.

**Auth / roles / middleware that actually runs**
`public` group: `RateLimitGlobal(RATE_LIMIT_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR)` (.env 100000/h, per-IP fixed window; it sets X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After headers). No auth.

**Handler:** `Backend/internal/adapter/http/handlers/policy_viewer_handler.go:120`. Service: `Backend/internal/core/usecases/platform_service.go:915`.

**Response 200 fields** (`data` is a map; values fall back to defaults if the setting is missing or invalid)
| name | type | source / default |
|---|---|---|
| anonymous_minutes_multiplier | float | platform_settings (category `booking`, key `anonymous_minutes_multiplier`). Accepted range 1–10. Default 2.0. |
| early_end_enabled | bool | (`session`,`early_end_enabled`), default false |
| early_end_approval_timeout_seconds | int | (`session`,`early_end_approval_timeout_seconds`), 30–600, default 120 |
| early_end_min_elapsed_minutes | int | constant `EarlyEndMinElapsedMinutes` = 10 |

- Fetch once at app start or booking-flow entry, and keep 2 as the fallback.
- Server-side the same setting is read by `WalletService.GetAnonymousMinutesMultiplier` (`wallet_service.go:1073`), with fallback `defaultAnonymousMinutesMultiplier = 2.0` (`booking_service.go:~3960`).
- The multiplier applies to the initial booking freeze (`booking_service.go:1377`), to every extension freeze and refund (`extensionFreezeMinutes`, `booking_service.go:3993`), and to the early-end/refund minute conversion (`walletMinutesForSessionMinutes`).

**Unresolved**
- The exact preview also needs `price_multiplier = solver_price_per_min / pricing.base_minute_value` (floored at 1). `base_minute_value` (platform_settings `pricing`/`base_minute_value`, default ₹5) is NOT exposed by any public endpoint found.
